name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data owning bfqq, bfqq is the queue being expired, compensate says whether the idle period is excluded from the measured service time, reason is a bfqq_expiration value; the caller is expected to hold bfqd->lock (the function takes no lock and takes or drops no reference itself). Postcondition: returns nothing. Steps in order: (1) slow = bfq_bfqq_is_slow(bfqd, bfqq, compensate, &delta) with delta starting at 0; for a non-sync bfqq that helper returns false immediately and leaves delta 0; for a sync bfqq it sets delta in every case (a minimum charge when the measured interval is under 1000 us, otherwise the interval in ms) and slow is BFQQ_SEEKY except that an interval over 20000 us gives slow = (bfqq->entity.service < bfq_max_budget/2). (2) Only if bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with bfq_bfqq_budget_left(bfqq) >= entity->budget/3) it calls bfq_bfqq_charge_time(bfqd, bfqq, delta). (3) If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1 it sets bfqq->last_wr_start_finish = jiffies. (4) If bfqd->low_latency, bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: dispatched == 0 sets soft_rt_next_start = bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start(); dispatched > 0 marks the softrt_update flag; a negative dispatched does neither. (5) It sets bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. (6) It calls __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) and then __bfq_bfqq_expire(bfqd, bfqq, reason); if the latter returns true (bfqq is gone) the function returns there (line 4417) without touching bfqq again. (7) Otherwise, if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED it marks bfqq non_blocking_wait_rq and leaves entity->service unchanged; in the else case it sets bfqq->entity.service = 0. (8) Finally it sets entity = entity->parent and runs for_each_entity(entity) entity->service = 0: with CONFIG_BFQ_GROUP_IOSCHED this clears every ancestor up the parent chain until NULL, without it only the single parent entity if non-NULL. Return points: line 4417 (early) and the end of the function.
note: slice cut the tail (lines 4432-4452, the parent-service reset loop). reviewer rounds 4 and 14 wrong: bfq-iosched.c:4449-4451 does reset parents' service via for_each_entity (macro at bfq-iosched.h:1105/1123). reviewer round 2 wrong: delta is the service-time interval (is_slow 4163-4180), idle excluded only when compensate. reviewer round 13 wrong: bfq_bfqq_is_slow returns false for non-sync at 4156-4157 before touching delta; delta is set in both interval branches (4173/4175/4180), not only when compensate. First reviewer (wr_coeff==1 charging) right and matches 4363-4367.

name: v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl
prose: Precondition: dir is the directory inode, dentry the (negative or in-lookup) dentry to open or create, file the struct file being opened, flags the open flags and omode the creation mode; this is the ->atomic_open operation for 9P2000.L (the function actually named v9fs_vfs_create_dotl at line 220 is a separate one-line wrapper that returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0)). Postcondition: returns an int. (a) If d_in_lookup(dentry), v9fs_vfs_lookup(dir, dentry, 0) is called; if it returns non-NULL res or the dentry is now positive, it returns finish_no_open(file, res) (line 245), which is PTR_ERR(res) when res is an error pointer and otherwise stores res in the file and returns 0. (b) If flags lacks O_CREAT it returns finish_no_open(file, NULL), i.e. 0 (line 250). (c) Otherwise it takes the parent fid with v9fs_parent_fid, clones it, computes the creation gid, adjusts the mode and ACLs with v9fs_acl_mode, rewrites a write-only open to read-write when the session has CACHE_WRITEBACK, creates the file with p9_client_create_dotl on the cloned fid, invalidates the directory attributes, walks to the new name with p9_client_walk, builds the inode with v9fs_get_new_inode_from_fid, sets the creation ACL, attaches the fid to the dentry, d_instantiates, and calls finish_open(file, dentry, generic_file_open). Each of those steps that can fail sets err and jumps to label out (lines 262, 270, 281, 293, 302, 308, 319): errors come from PTR_ERR of the fid/inode, from v9fs_acl_mode, from p9_client_create_dotl (err < 0) and from finish_open. On success it stores ofid in file->private_data, optionally takes an fscache cookie, calls v9fs_fid_add_modes and v9fs_open_fid_add(inode, &ofid) and sets FMODE_CREATED in file->f_mode, then falls into out. Label out (reached on every path of step (c), success or error) calls p9_fid_put on dfid, ofid and fid (which ignore NULL and error pointers; ofid and fid are passed by address to the *_add helpers earlier) and v9fs_put_acl(dacl, pacl), then returns err, which is 0 on success. A failure after the file was created on the server (walk, inode, finish_open) returns an error without removing it.
note: slice cut the head (lines 226-251; function starts at 227); the packet name v9fs_vfs_create_dotl was the 5-line wrapper at 220, wrong item. reviewers: round 5 wrong (create_dotl and finish_open are indeed called, 289 and 317; my prose agrees), round 12 right-ish (positive lookup only returns early if res non-NULL or dentry positive after lookup, 244-245), round 13 right (finish_no_open(file,dentry) variant no, but O_CREAT unset returns finish_no_open(file,NULL)=0 at 250, claim of -ENOENT wrong), round 14 wrong: finish_no_open returns 0 or PTR_ERR(dentry) (open.c:1072-1077), not 1.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Precondition: vc is a volume-location cursor owned by one task; on the first call vc->nr_iterations is -1, on later calls vc->alist, vc->addr_index, vc->addr_tried, vc->call_error, vc->call_abort_code and vc->call_responded describe the previous attempt. Postcondition: returns true when it has selected an address to try, false when no further attempt should be made. It increments vc->nr_iterations first (line 102), so that happens on every return including the stopped one. Return points: (1) false at line 111 if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set, with nothing else changed. (2) For a later call (nr_iterations != 0) it stores vc->call_error into alist->addrs[addr_index].last_error and switches on the error: 0 or any error not listed (default) sets cumul_error.error = error, sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP and returns false (line 127), keeping vc->alist and vc->server_list references; -ECONNABORTED with abort codes AFSVL_IO/BADVOLOPER/NOMEM records -EREMOTEIO via afs_prioritise_error and goes to next_server, any other abort code records the error and goes to failed; the connection-type errors (-ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME) are recorded and go to iterate_address; -ECONNRESET is recorded, sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY and goes to next_server; -EOPNOTSUPP goes to next_server without recording. (3) true at line 278: iterate_address ANDs alist->responded with the complement of probe_failed and addr_tried; if the set is empty it goes to next_server, otherwise it takes alist->preferred when that bit is in the set else the lowest set bit, marks it in addr_tried, stores addr_index and vc->alist, clears vc->call_responded and returns true. (4) false at line 318 via failed: if an alist is held it is put (after optionally updating alist->preferred) and vc->alist set to NULL, then AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is set; reached from the abort case, from a failure of afs_start_vl_iteration, afs_send_vl_probes (error < 0 recorded) or afs_wait_for_vl_probes (error < 0 recorded), from a second restart when AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRIED is already set, and from no_more_servers when RETRY is not set. Other paths: next_server puts the current address list (optionally updating preferred) and goes to pick_server; pick_server waits for probes, prefers server_list->preferred if untried, otherwise picks the untried responding server with the lowest rtt, else goes to no_more_servers; selected_server clears its untried bit, sets vc->server, takes a reference on the server's address list under vlserver->lock, zeros addr_tried and sets addr_index to -1; no_more_servers goes to restart_from_beginning if AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY is set (puts alist and server_list, NULLs them, sets RETRIED) else records each server's responded flag and probe error into cumul_error before failed. First call (nr_iterations == 0) jumps to start, skipping the result evaluation.
note: slice cut the tail (lines 253-319, the address selection and failure paths). reviewer round 1 right (default/STOP false return leaves alist and server_list references: line 127 returns before any put). round 2 half right: addr_index/addr_tried are set to the chosen address at 269-271 (right) but the no-servers false path does go through afs_prioritise_error on each server at 298-305 (so cumul_error can be set there; wrong in that part). round 6 right: nr_iterations++ at 102 precedes the STOP check at 109. round 16 plausibly right: restart (182) nulls server_list, and afs_start_vl_iteration (190) can fail; I make no claim about server_list being NULL.

name: aio_poll_wake
prose: Precondition: wait is the wait_queue_entry embedded in the poll_iocb of a live aio_kiocb; it is called from the waitqueue wake-up path with the waitqueue lock held; key is the poll mask (possibly 0 for a plain wakeup). Postcondition: returns 0 at line 1797 if mask is non-zero and shares no bit with req->events, with nothing else done. Otherwise it returns 1 at line 1866 after one of two actions. (a) If mask is non-zero, req->work_scheduled is false and spin_trylock_irqsave(&ctx->ctx_lock) succeeds: it removes the wait entry (list_del_init) and the kiocb from ctx->ki_list, sets ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask); if ki_eventfd is set and eventfd_signal_allowed() is false it instead sets iocb to NULL and schedules aio_poll_put_work on req->work; it then unlocks, and calls iocb_put(iocb) only if iocb is still non-NULL. (b) Otherwise (mask 0, work already scheduled, or the trylock failed): if work_scheduled it sets work_need_resched = true, else it schedule_work()s req->work and sets work_scheduled = true; and if mask contains POLLFREE it also sets req->cancelled, removes the wait entry and finally does smp_store_release(&req->head, NULL). The wait entry is not removed from the waitqueue in case (b) unless POLLFREE is set.
note: unreviewed; checked against aio.c:1787-1867. Original reviewer claim (returns 0 on event mismatch; work not scheduled if already scheduled) is right: 1796-1797 and 1837-1838.

name: aio_poll
prose: Precondition: aiocb is an initialised aio_kiocb with ki_ctx valid and the poll file set; iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block; the caller holds no ctx_lock (the function takes it with spin_lock_irq). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL at line 1904 if aio_buf has bits outside the low 16 bits, or at 1907 if aio_offset, aio_nbytes or aio_rw_flags is non-zero, before changing the request. Otherwise it initialises the poll_iocb (work function aio_poll_complete_work, events = demangle_poll(aio_buf) | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP, head NULL, cancelled/work_scheduled/work_need_resched false), sets apt.error = -EINVAL, installs aio_poll_wake as the wake function, and calls vfs_poll; mask is the returned events masked with req->events. If aio_poll_queue_proc queued the request (apt.queued): under poll_iocb_lock_wq, if the request is no longer on the queue or work is already scheduled then (if apt.error was still non-zero) cancel is set, apt.error = 0 and mask = 0 (wake already scheduled the work or completed the request); then if mask or apt.error is non-zero the wait entry is removed (synchronous completion/steal), else if cancel the request is marked cancelled, else if still on the queue the kiocb is added to ctx->active_reqs with ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel. If mask is still non-zero, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask) and apt.error = 0; after unlocking, iocb_put(aiocb) runs only when mask is non-zero. It returns apt.error (line 1966): 0 for a request left waiting, completed by a wake, or completed synchronously; otherwise whatever apt.error holds, which stays -EINVAL if nothing was queued (file has no poll support) and may be an error set by aio_poll_queue_proc.
note: unreviewed; checked against aio.c:1894-1967. Original reviewer claim (omits cancel path returning 0 without active_reqs or synchronous completion) right: 1937-1939 and 1945-1947 give return 0 without adding to active_reqs.

name: __io_submit_one
prose: Precondition: ctx is the kioctx, iocb the kernel copy of the user control block, user_iocb its user address, req an aio_kiocb from aio_get_req, compat selects the compat layout. Postcondition: returns an int. -EBADF if fget(iocb->aio_fildes) returns NULL (line 1975; req->ki_filp is NULL). If IOCB_FLAG_RESFD is set and eventfd_ctx_fdget fails it returns PTR_ERR of that (1987); otherwise req->ki_eventfd is set. -EFAULT if put_user of KIOCB_KEY into user_iocb->aio_key fails (1994). Otherwise it fills ki_res.obj/data and zeroes res/res2, and dispatches on aio_lio_opcode, returning the value of aio_read (PREAD, PREADV with vectored flag), aio_write (PWRITE, PWRITEV), aio_fsync (FSYNC, FDSYNC, with datasync flag) or aio_poll (POLL), or -EINVAL (2019) for any other opcode. On the early error returns the function does not release ki_filp or ki_eventfd itself; whoever calls it (io_submit_one) is responsible for the cleanup of req, and on the dispatch returns ownership of the request follows the handler (asynchronous completion may happen after the return).
note: unreviewed; checked against aio.c:1969-2021. Cleanup of req is not in this function (no fput/eventfd_ctx_put/kmem_cache_free here), so the prose does not claim it. Round-1 reviewer (caller does not free req on success; handler/async completion owns it) matches the dispatch returns; stated carefully, not asserted for specific handlers.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit, aio_context_t, ctx_id, long, nr,
prose: Generated system call io_submit(ctx_id, nr, iocbpp) (aio.c:2082-2121). Precondition: iocbpp is a user pointer to an array of nr user pointers to struct iocb; may sleep. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if nr < 0 (line 2091) or if lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context (2096), in both cases without any other effect. Otherwise nr is clamped to ctx->nr_events, a block plug is started when nr > AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD, and for i from 0 to nr-1 it does get_user of the i-th iocb pointer (on failure ret = -EFAULT and the loop stops) and calls io_submit_one(ctx, user_iocb, false) (a non-zero return stops the loop with ret set); the plug is finished if it was started and the reference on ctx taken by lookup_ioctx is dropped with percpu_ref_put. It returns i if at least one iocb was submitted (i is the number of iocbs completed before the loop stopped, so a failure after some successes is hidden), otherwise ret (0 if nr == 0, or the error of the first iocb).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel, aio_context_t, ctx_id, struct iocb __user *, iocb,
prose: Generated system call io_cancel(ctx_id, iocb, result) (aio.c:2176-2216); result is not used. Precondition: iocb is a user pointer to a control block previously passed to io_submit. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if get_user of iocb->aio_key fails (2186), -EINVAL if the key differs from KIOCB_KEY (2188) or lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context (2192). Otherwise it takes ctx->ctx_lock with spin_lock_irq and walks ctx->active_reqs for the entry whose ki_res.obj equals the user pointer; for the first match it calls kiocb->ki_cancel(&kiocb->rw), keeps its return in ret, does list_del_init on the entry and stops. After unlocking, if ret is 0 it is replaced by -EINPROGRESS (the completion is delivered through the ring); the context reference is dropped with percpu_ref_put and ret is returned. ret starts as -EINVAL, so it returns -EINVAL when no active request matches, and otherwise returns -EINPROGRESS when ki_cancel returned 0 or ki_cancel's non-zero value.

name: BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64);
prose: The macro invocation BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64) (accessors.h:265, macro defined at accessors.h:62-74) generates two static inline functions, each starting with a compile-time check that the member is exactly 64 bits wide: u64 btrfs_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, const struct btrfs_inode_item *s) and void btrfs_set_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, struct btrfs_inode_item *s, u64 val). Precondition: eb is a valid extent buffer and s is the offset of an inode item inside eb, represented as a pointer value (not a dereferenceable address). Postcondition, getter: it has a single return statement, return btrfs_get_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size)). With member_offset = (unsigned long)s + offsetof(size): if member_offset + 8 > eb->len, btrfs_get_64 issues a btrfs_warn bounds report and returns 0; otherwise it returns the 64-bit little-endian value stored at that offset (read across two folios when the field straddles a folio boundary). The getter does not modify the buffer. Postcondition, setter: it returns nothing and calls btrfs_set_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size), val). If member_offset + 8 > eb->len it issues the same bounds warning and writes nothing; otherwise it stores val in little-endian byte order at that offset (split across two folios when the field straddles a boundary), which modifies the extent buffer contents (the const qualifier on eb applies to the descriptor, not the data). Neither function takes a lock, takes or drops a reference, allocates memory or marks the buffer dirty.

Only the name changed to the exact macro invocation at accessors.h:265 (it was 'btrfs_inode_size (BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS family)').

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is a transaction handle of trans->fs_info with trans->use_count 1 (ASSERT); cur_trans = trans->transaction. The handle is consumed on every return: ended by btrfs_end_transaction, freed after a completed commit, or freed in cleanup_transaction. Postcondition: returns an int through four return statements (transaction.c:2298, 2616, 2635, 2645). Start: it clears BTRFS_FS_NEED_TRANS_COMMIT; if cur_trans is aborted, ret = cur_trans->aborted and it goes to lockdep_trans_commit_start_release (releases the COMMIT_PREP lockdep state, calls btrfs_end_transaction(trans) and returns ret: return at 2645). Otherwise it releases the handle's metadata reservation (btrfs_trans_release_metadata), sets trans->block_rsv = NULL, and if it wins test_and_set_bit of BTRFS_DELAYED_REFS_FLUSHING it runs btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0) (non-zero: goto lockdep_trans_commit_start_release, return 2645). It calls btrfs_create_pending_block_groups; if BTRFS_TRANS_DIRTY_BG_RUN is not yet set it sets it under ro_block_group_mutex and, for the task that set it, runs btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups (non-zero: lockdep_trans_commit_start_release, return 2645). Under trans_lock: (A) if cur_trans->state >= COMMIT_PREP (another task is already committing) it add_pending_snapshot(trans), drops the lock, takes a reference on cur_trans, sets want_state to COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED when trans->in_fsync), releases the lockdep state, ret = btrfs_end_transaction(trans), wait_for_commit(cur_trans, want_state), replaces ret by cur_trans->aborted if the transaction is aborted, drops its reference and returns ret (return 2298). (B) Otherwise it becomes the committer: state = COMMIT_PREP, wakes waiters; if cur_trans is not first on fs_info->trans_list and the previous transaction's state is below want_state it takes a reference on it, drops trans_lock, waits for it, takes ret = prev_trans->aborted, puts it and goes to lockdep_release on non-zero ret, else retakes the lock; if cur_trans is first on the list and BTRFS_FS_ERROR is set it drops the lock and goes to lockdep_release with ret = -EROFS. Then state = COMMIT_START, trans_lock dropped, critical_section_start_time recorded, the external-writer count decremented, ret = btrfs_start_delalloc_flush (non-zero: lockdep_release) and ret = btrfs_run_delayed_items(trans) (non-zero: lockdep_release). It then releases the extwriters lockdep map, waits for the external writer count to reach 0, runs btrfs_run_delayed_items again (non-zero: releases the writers lockdep map and goes directly to cleanup_transaction), calls btrfs_wait_delalloc_flush, waits for pending_ordered to reach 0, calls btrfs_scrub_pause, then under trans_lock add_pending_snapshot(trans) and state = COMMIT_DOING, releases the writers lockdep map and waits for num_writers == 1, acquires three state lockdep maps and clears BTRFS_FS_COMMIT_TRANS. If the transaction is aborted it sets ret = cur_trans->aborted, releases the UNBLOCKED lockdep state and goes to scrub_continue. Otherwise it takes reloc_mutex and runs create_pending_snapshots, btrfs_run_delayed_items, btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, U64_MAX), commit_fs_roots, then btrfs_free_log_root_tree, btrfs_qgroup_account_extents (negative result fails) and commit_cowonly_roots; a failure (non-zero, negative for qgroup) goes to unlock_reloc with ret set, and an abort noticed after commit_cowonly_roots sets ret = cur_trans->aborted and goes to unlock_reloc. It then sets cur_trans = fs_info->running_transaction, adds the tree root and chunk root to switch_commits, calls switch_commit_roots and update_super_roots, zeroes the super copy's log root and level, copies super_copy to super_for_commit, calls btrfs_commit_device_sizes, clears BTRFS_FS_LOG1_ERR and LOG2_ERR, releases chunk metadata and takes tree_log_mutex. Under trans_lock state = UNBLOCKED and fs_info->running_transaction = NULL; reloc_mutex is released and waiters woken; the cleaner kthread is woken if BTRFS_FS_FEATURE_CHANGED is set. btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction failing calls btrfs_handle_fs_error, unlocks tree_log_mutex and goes to scrub_continue; write_all_supers(fs_info, 0) is followed by unlocking tree_log_mutex and a non-zero result goes to scrub_continue (no btrfs_handle_fs_error there). Then update_commit_stats, state = SUPER_COMMITTED, btrfs_finish_extent_commit (non-zero: scrub_continue), btrfs_clear_space_info_full if BTRFS_TRANS_HAVE_FREE_BGS is set, btrfs_set_last_trans_committed, state = COMPLETED, removal of cur_trans from trans_list under trans_lock, two btrfs_put_transaction calls on cur_trans, sb_end_intwrite if trans->type has __TRANS_FREEZABLE, btrfs_scrub_continue, current->journal_info cleared if it equals trans, the handle freed, and return ret, which is 0 here (return 2616). Error labels: unlock_reloc releases reloc_mutex and the UNBLOCKED lockdep state and falls into scrub_continue, which releases two lockdep states, calls btrfs_scrub_continue and falls into cleanup_transaction: btrfs_trans_release_metadata, btrfs_cleanup_pending_block_groups, btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata, trans->block_rsv = NULL, a btrfs_warn 'Skipping commit of aborted transaction.', current->journal_info cleared if it equals trans, then the static cleanup_transaction(trans, ret) and return ret (2635; ret is the error). lockdep_release releases the extwriters and writers lockdep maps and goes to cleanup_transaction directly, without btrfs_scrub_continue.

Return statements verified: 2298, 2616, 2635, 2645. I did not verify what btrfs_start_delalloc_flush does internally, so no claim about it.

name: ceph_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open ceph directory whose private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info (dfi), ctx is a valid dir_context, and the caller holds no ceph spinlock; this is the iterate_shared handler (dir.c:317-639). Postcondition: returns an int; the return statements are: (1) 0 at line 333 if CEPH_F_ATEND is set in dfi->file_info.flags. (2) 0 at 341 if ctx->pos == 0 and dir_emit of '.' refuses, else ctx->pos becomes 1. (3) 0 at 355 if ctx->pos == 1 and dir_emit of '..' (parent inode read under dentry->d_lock) refuses, else ctx->pos becomes 2. (4) the negative result of ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir at 361. The code then touches the file mode under i_ceph_lock and, when the DCACHE mount option is on, NOASYNCREADDIR is off, the inode is not the snapdir, the directory is complete and ordered and the shared-cap is issued, calls __dcache_readdir; (5) any result other than -EAGAIN of that call is returned at 378 (-EAGAIN falls through to the normal path). In the fetch loop (label more), when need_send_readdir() says the buffered frag is not the right one, it drops any old dfi->last_readdir, picks a frag and creates an MDS request: (6) PTR_ERR(req) at 411 if ceph_mdsc_create_request fails; (7) the error of ceph_alloc_readdir_reply_buffer at 416 after ceph_mdsc_put_request(req); (8) -ENOMEM at 431 if kzalloc of req->r_path2 fails (req put); (9) a negative result of ceph_encode_encrypted_dname at 438 (req put); (10) a negative result of ceph_mdsc_do_request at 459 (req put). On success the reply is parsed, dfi->frag and dfi->last_readdir are updated (the request is kept in dfi->last_readdir), readdir-cache and dir-release/ordered counters are set or cleared depending on CEPH_MDS_R_DID_PREPOPULATE, and if the reply has entries note_last_dentry is called with the last name; (11) a non-zero result of it is returned at 515 after the request is put and dfi->last_readdir cleared. The function then binary-searches the reply entries for the first whose offset is not below ctx->pos and loops over the rest: (12) -EIO at 551 if an entry has rde->offset < ctx->pos, with last_readdir put and cleared; (13) -EIO at 557 if the entry has no inode (rde->inode.in NULL, with a WARN_ON_ONCE), also with last_readdir put and cleared; for each entry ctx->pos is set to rde->offset, and (14) 0 is returned at 575 if dir_emit refuses (the buffer is full), leaving dfi->last_readdir kept for the next call; otherwise ctx->pos is incremented. After the loop dfi->last_readdir is put and cleared; if dfi->next_offset > 2 it goes back to more with the same frag; else if dfi->frag is not the rightmost it moves to the next frag (setting ctx->pos to the new frag position, and freeing dfi->last_name in the non-hash-order case) and goes to more; otherwise it sets CEPH_F_ATEND and, if i_release_count still equals dfi->dir_release_count, under i_ceph_lock updates i_size from readdir_cache_idx when the ordered count also matches (BUG_ON if readdir_cache_idx < 0 there) and calls __ceph_dir_set_complete; (15) returns 0 at 638.
note: slice cut head (slice 267-522, function 317-639) and tail. reviewers: original (returns 0 when dir_emit fails) right (341/355/575). round 2 (omits -ENOMEM for r_path2) right (431). rounds 10, 12, 13 wrong: dir.c:545-552 returns -EIO when rde->offset < ctx->pos, it does not skip; round 10 'drops the reply and reply retained on full buffer' wrong on retention: last_readdir is kept at 575. round 16 wrong: the -EIO condition at 545 is offset < pos, not offset != pos.

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits; path is the extent-tree path from ext4_find_extent for newext's logical block, valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode); newext points to the extent to insert and its range does not overlap an existing extent; gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Postcondition: returns a struct ext4_ext_path pointer (the original path, or the replacement path when the next leaf was used) or an ERR_PTR; the return statements are 'return path' at extents.c:2140 (ext4_ext_create_new_leaf returned an error pointer, which is passed on as is), 'return path' at 2216 on success, and 'return ERR_PTR(err)' at 2220 after errout frees the current path with ext4_free_ext_path. The paths to errout are: zero actual length of newext (EXT4_ERROR_INODE, err = -EFSCORRUPTED, 2010-2013), a NULL path[depth].p_hdr (-EFSCORRUPTED, 2018-2022), failure of ext4_ext_get_access in an append, prepend or has_space step, failure of ext4_find_extent for the next leaf (err = PTR_ERR), and failure of ext4_ext_correct_indexes or ext4_ext_dirty. Behaviour: if there is a nearest extent ex and EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO is not set (line 2025, so with PRE_IO or no ex the whole block is skipped), it picks the right or left neighbour of ex as appropriate and tries to append newext to ex (ext4_can_extents_be_merged), else to prepend it; a successful merge gets journal access, extends ex (keeping its unwritten mark; a prepend also takes newext's block and physical block) and goes to merge. Otherwise, if the leaf has room (eh_entries < eh_max) it goes to has_space; if full and newext lies beyond the last extent it looks at the next leaf (ext4_find_extent, BUG_ON on depth mismatch) and uses it, freeing the old path, if that leaf has room, else frees npath; if there is still no room it sets EXT4_MB_USE_RESERVED when EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_METADATA_NOFAIL is set and calls ext4_ext_create_new_leaf. At has_space it gets journal access, and either uses the first slot (no extent in the leaf) or inserts before or after nearex, with BUG_ON when the block numbers are equal, memmove-ing following extents; it increments eh_entries, sets path[depth].p_ext and copies newext in. At merge it calls ext4_ext_try_to_merge unless PRE_IO is set, then ext4_ext_correct_indexes and ext4_ext_dirty.
note: slice cut head (function at 1997-2221, slice 2046-2300): name outside slice. reviewers rounds 11-13 wrong: PRE_IO skips the whole append/prepend block at extents.c:2025 as well as ext4_ext_try_to_merge at 2204. round 14 wrong: the zero-length and NULL p_hdr cases do goto errout (2013, 2021), which returns ERR_PTR(err) at 2220 after freeing the path, not an immediate return.

name: ext4_free_data
prose: Precondition: handle is a journal handle for inode's filesystem, first and last delimit a run of __le32 block pointers (in the inode or in the indirect block this_bh), first <= last, and this_bh is NULL for pointers in the inode or the buffer holding them otherwise (indirect.c:914-985, static void). Postcondition: returns nothing. If this_bh is non-NULL it first calls ext4_journal_get_write_access on it and returns immediately on error (line 935) without freeing anything. It then scans p from first up to (not including) last, skipping zero pointers, grouping consecutive pointers whose block numbers are contiguous into a run, and for each run that ends it calls ext4_clear_blocks(handle, inode, this_bh, run start, count, first pointer of the run, current p), which zeroes those pointers and frees the blocks, or returns 1 without freeing when the block range is invalid (reporting EXT4_ERROR_INODE), or a negative error. A non-zero result stops the scan; after the loop, if there was no error and a run is pending, it is cleared the same way. If the result is negative (err < 0) it returns (line 966) without marking the buffer dirty; a positive result (the invalid-range case) does not return early. Finally, if this_bh is non-NULL it calls ext4_handle_dirty_metadata(handle, inode, this_bh) when the inode has no journal or the buffer has a journal head, else reports 'circular indirect block detected' with EXT4_ERROR_INODE and does not dirty it.
note: slice does not contain the function at all (slice 1306-1474, function at indirect.c:914-985): name outside slice; fixed from real source. reviewer round 15 wrong: the function is static void (indirect.c:914) and has no return value; and first/last/this_bh are its parameters (914-916). The reviewer's point that the prose should not have called it int-returning is moot. Contract left empty: pointer parameters.

name: ext4_ind_map_blocks
prose: Precondition: inode is an ext4 inode mapped with indirect blocks (EXT4_INODE_EXTENTS clear, ASSERT), map->m_lblk and m_len give the logical range, handle may be NULL only when EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CREATE is not set (ASSERT), flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags (indirect.c:530-673). Postcondition: returns an int err. It starts with err = -EIO and computes the block path with ext4_block_to_path; depth 0 (block number out of range) jumps to out and returns -EIO with map unchanged. Otherwise ext4_get_branch fills chain and err (0, or -EIO/-EFSCORRUPTED/-ENOMEM if reading or validating an indirect block failed) and returns partial. (a) partial == NULL (block mapped): it counts how many following blocks are physically contiguous (bounded by map->m_len and blocks_to_boundary), then got_it. (b) partial non-NULL and EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CREATE not set: it computes the size of the hole below partial, sets map->m_pblk = 0 and map->m_len = umin(map->m_len, hole size), and goes to cleanup, returning whatever err ext4_get_branch left: 0 for a plain hole, or the read/validation error (so a failed indirect-block read returns -EIO, not 0, in this path). (c) CREATE set and err == -EIO: goto cleanup, returns -EIO (other get_branch errors such as -EFSCORRUPTED or -ENOMEM do not stop here and fall through to allocation, where err is overwritten). (d) bigalloc feature: EXT4_ERROR_INODE and err = -EFSCORRUPTED, goto out. (e) Allocation: builds an ext4_allocation_request (goal from ext4_find_goal, length from ext4_blks_to_allocate), calls ext4_alloc_branch and, if that returned 0, ext4_splice_branch; a non-zero err goes to cleanup and is returned; on success it sets EXT4_MAP_NEW, updates the fsync transaction, count = ar.len. got_it: sets EXT4_MAP_MAPPED, m_pblk to the leaf key, m_len = count, EXT4_MAP_BOUNDARY if count > blocks_to_boundary, and err = count (the positive number of mapped blocks). cleanup releases (brelse) the buffer heads of the chain from partial down to (but not including) chain[0]; out traces and returns err. So the return is the number of blocks mapped (> 0), 0 for a hole, or a negative error.
note: slice cut head (function at 530-673, slice 545-796 reaches into the next function). reviewer round 15 wrong: ext4_get_branch sets *err = ret (-EIO, -EFSCORRUPTED or -ENOMEM) at indirect.c:191-192 and the non-CREATE path at 575-592 goes to cleanup returning that err, so an indirect-block read failure is not turned into 0. Prose keeps the -EIO claim but qualified.

name: ext4_do_writepages
prose: Precondition: mpd, mpd->wbc and mpd->inode are valid and mpd->inode->i_mapping is the mapping to write back; the caller holds no folio locks and no journal handle (inode.c:2783-3032, static int). Postcondition: has a single return, 'return ret' at 3031 after label out_writepages, which first calls trace_ext4_writepages_result; ret is 0 or a negative error. Early exits to out_writepages (skipping the writeback_index update at 3021-3026): the mapping has no pages or no dirty tag (ret 0, line 2806); ext4_emergency_state(sb) returns non-zero (ret is that value, 2818-2820); ext4_journal_start fails while clearing inline data (ret = PTR_ERR, 2832). Otherwise: if the inode has inline data it starts a one-credit handle, destroys the inline data and stops the handle. In data=journal mode it sets mpd->can_map = 0 and, for WB_SYNC_ALL, calls ext4_fc_commit on the inode's datasync tid. It sets mpd->journalled_more_data = 0, computes rsv_blocks when dioread_nolock is in use, sets range_whole, and takes the start/end positions from the cyclic writeback_index or from wbc->range_start/range_end (cycled = 0 when range_cyclic and writeback_index is non-zero). At retry it tags pages for WB_SYNC_ALL or tagged_writepages, starts a plug, and does a first pass with mpd->do_map = 0 using an io_end (ext4_init_io_end failure: ret = -ENOMEM, goto unplug), mpage_prepare_extent_to_map, release of unused pages and submission; a negative result goes to unplug. Then, while !mpd->scanned_until_end and wbc->nr_to_write > 0, each iteration allocates an io_end (-ENOMEM breaks), starts a handle with ext4_journal_start_with_reserve (failure: ret = PTR_ERR, message, io_end put, break), sets do_map = 1, calls mpage_prepare_extent_to_map and, if that returned 0 and mpd->map.m_len is non-zero, mpage_map_and_submit_extent; stops the handle (immediately when it is not synchronous, else after dropping the io_end reference with ext4_put_io_end_defer), releases unused pages, submits the IO and drops the io_end. Then ret == -ENOSPC with a journal forces a commit (jbd2_journal_force_commit_nested), sets ret = 0 and continues; -EAGAIN becomes 0; any other non-zero ret breaks. At unplug it finishes the plug; if ret is 0, cycled is 0 and nr_to_write > 0 it sets cycled = 1, end_pos to just below the old writeback_index, start_pos = 0 and jumps back to retry. Finally, if wbc->range_cyclic is set, or range_whole is set and nr_to_write > 0, it sets mapping->writeback_index = mpd->start_pos >> PAGE_SHIFT (done on the error exits from the loop too, but not on the early exits above).
note: slice cut head (function at 2783-3032, slice 2798-3049). reviewer round 15 right: writeback_index is not updated on the early gotos at 2806, 2820, 2832 (update at 3021-3026 is after them), and the emergency-state return value at 2818-2820 was omitted. Single return at 3031.

name: __ext4_iget
prose: Precondition: sb is a mounted ext4 superblock with valid s_es and journal pointer, ino is the inode number, flags is a combination of EXT4_IGET_* (SPECIAL, HANDLE, NOWAIT, EA_INODE, ...), function and line identify the caller for error reports (inode.c:5227-5609). Postcondition: returns a struct inode pointer (a fully read inode, either already cached or newly initialised and unlocked) or an ERR_PTR. Return points: (1) ERR_PTR(-ESTALE) at 5248 if ino is out of range (a special inode without EXT4_IGET_SPECIAL, below EXT4_ROOT_INO, or above s_inodes_count) and EXT4_IGET_HANDLE is set (silently); without HANDLE, ERR_PTR(-EFSCORRUPTED) at 5252 after a __ext4_error report. (2) With EXT4_IGET_NOWAIT: ERR_PTR(-ENOENT) at 5258 when find_inode_nowait finds no inode, or at 5265 if after waiting on a new inode it is unhashed (iput first); without NOWAIT, iget_locked returning NULL gives ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) at 5270. (3) If the inode was already initialised (I_NEW clear), check_igot_inode is run: non-zero returns ERR_PTR(that value) after iput (5277), zero returns the cached inode (5279). (4) For a new inode it reads the on-disk inode with __ext4_get_inode_loc_noinmem and validates and decodes it; every failure sets ret and goes to bad_inode (brelse of iloc.bh, iget_failed(inode), return ERR_PTR(ret) at 5608): the location read error (negative ret); -ESTALE under EXT4_IGET_HANDLE when i_links_count and i_mode are both 0; -EFSCORRUPTED for a bad i_extra_isize (too large or not a multiple of 4); -EFSBADCRC (not -EFSCORRUPTED) when the inode checksum fails and no fast-commit replay is in progress; for i_nlink == 0 on an unallocated/deleted inode (not the boot loader inode): -EFSCORRUPTED if EXT4_IGET_SPECIAL else -ESTALE; -EFSCORRUPTED for both INLINE_DATA and EXTENTS flags, for i_size < 0 or above ext4_get_maxbytes, for an INDEX directory without dir_index under metadata_csum, for a bad xattr block number, for a bad immutable/append flag on a symlink, for an invalid orphan or fast symlink length, for a bogus i_mode (other than the boot loader inode, which is made bad with make_bad_inode and is not an error here), and for a casefold flag without the feature; the result of ext4_iget_extra_inode, ext4_ext_check_inode or ext4_ind_check_inode when non-zero. It sets the file, directory, symlink or special-inode operations by mode, caches fast-symlink targets, sets the sync tids from the journal, and calls ext4_set_inode_mapping_order. (5) Finally check_igot_inode is run again: ret == -ESTALE does brelse, unlock_new_inode, iput and returns ERR_PTR(-ESTALE) at 5596 (not via bad_inode); other non-zero ret goes to bad_inode; on success it does brelse, unlock_new_inode and returns the inode at 5603.
note: slice cut head (function at 5227-5609, slice 5094-5350). reviewers: original (omits -ENOENT for NOWAIT and -EFSCORRUPTED from check_igot_inode / bad extra_isize) right (5258, 5265, 5306, 5587-5599). round 2 right: checksum failure returns -EFSBADCRC (5328). round 15 right: with EXT4_IGET_HANDLE the out-of-range case returns -ESTALE without __ext4_error (5247-5248).

name: __mb_check_buddy
prose: The caller holds the ext4 group lock for e4b->bd_group and e4b is a valid buddy descriptor whose bd_sb, bd_info, bd_group and bd_blkbits are valid and whose buddy cache is initialized (EXT4_MB_GRP_NEED_INIT(e4b->bd_info) is false) with valid bb_counters, bb_first_free, bb_fragments and bb_prealloc_list. The function increments e4b->bd_info->bb_check_counter and, if the new value is not a multiple of 10, returns immediately without further checks; otherwise it performs the integrity checks and returns normally only if they all pass — for each order from bd_blkbits+1 down to 2, mb_find_buddy returns non-NULL distinct buddies with max*2 == max2, for every allocated (1) higher-order bit at most one of its two lower-order bits is free (0), and bb_counters[order] equals the number of free (0) higher-order bits; then, using the order-0 buddy, every free (0) order-0 bit has index >= bb_first_free, bb_fragments equals the number of runs of free order-0 bits, and for each even order-0 index i the number of free bits among k = i>>j for j = 1..bd_blkbits+1 (with k < max2 asserted) is 0 when either bit of the pair (i, i+1) is allocated and 1 when both are free, and EXT4_MB_GRP_NEED_INIT(e4b->bd_info) is false; after that, if ext4_get_group_info(sb, e4b->bd_group) returns NULL it returns without the prealloc-list checks, otherwise for every prealloc space on grp->bb_prealloc_list with nonzero pa_len, pa_pstart lies in e4b->bd_group and all pa_len order-0 bits starting at its group offset are allocated (1), after which it returns; any failed MB_CHECK_ASSERT prints a KERN_EMERG message and calls BUG(), so the function does not return in that case.
note: unreviewed; existing prose checked line by line against mballoc.c:703-793: return at 722 when bb_check_counter++ % 10 is non-zero; order loop 724-748 (asserts at 726-730, 746); bit test 735-741 matches 'at most one lower free bit'; 0 = free (counted at 744); order-0 pass 750-777; return at 781 if ext4_get_group_info is NULL; prealloc check 782-792. All correct. Original reviewer wrong ('at most one' is what 737-739 checks) and round 2 reviewer wrong (set bit = allocated, 735 skips it, 744 counts clear bits as free). Added fact not in prose: the function exists only under AGGRESSIVE_CHECK (mballoc.c:673-798), where MB_CHECK_ASSERT is the printk+BUG macro.

name: move_extent_per_page
prose: Precondition: o_filp is open on the original inode, donor_inode is the donor inode, orig_page_offset and donor_page_offset are page indexes, data_offset_in_page and block_len_in_page select the block range within the page, unwritten says whether the original range was unwritten, err points to an int the caller owns (move_extent.c:259-443). Postcondition: returns int replaced_count (blocks whose extents were swapped) and reports failure through *err; the two return statements are 'return 0' at 288 and 'return replaced_count' at 422. *err is set to 0 at the top of each attempt (label again). If ext4_journal_start (credits from ext4_meta_trans_blocks * 2) fails it sets *err = PTR_ERR(handle) and returns 0 (288). Otherwise it computes the byte count to replace (the last block of the file may be partial), locks both folios with mext_folio_double_lock (negative result: goto stop_journal). If unwritten is set it takes both i_data_sem for write, rechecks extent coverage on both inodes with mext_check_coverage (an error goes to drop_data_sem); if some extent became initialised it drops the semaphores and falls back to the data_copy path; otherwise it needs both folios releasable (filemap_release_folio) else *err = -EBUSY, and calls ext4_swap_extents; either way it drops the semaphores and goes to unlock_folios without copying. data_copy path: mext_page_mkuptodate on the original folio (non-zero *err: unlock_folios), release both folios' buffers (else *err = -EBUSY), then ext4_swap_extents under both semaphores; if it sets *err and replaced_count is 0 it goes to unlock_folios, if replaced_count is non-zero it continues with that smaller block count. It then calls ext4_get_block per block (a negative result stores *err and goes to repair_branches, below), block_commit_write on the original folio, and sets *err = ext4_jbd2_inode_add_write(...) (overwriting any earlier *err from the swap), then falls into unlock_folios (unlock and put both folios) and stop_journal (ext4_journal_stop). After stopping the handle, if *err == -ENOSPC and ext4_should_retry_alloc says so it goes to again; if *err == -EBUSY, retries++ < 4, a journal exists and jbd2_journal_force_commit_nested returns non-zero it also goes to again; otherwise returns replaced_count (422). repair_branches: swaps the extents back (donor to original, ext4_swap_extents with the last argument 0); if the number replaced differs from block_len_in_page it reports EXT4_ERROR 'Unable to copy data block, data will be lost.' and sets *err = -EIO; replaced_count is then set to 0 and it goes to unlock_folios. So a non-zero return can coexist with a negative *err (for example when ext4_jbd2_inode_add_write fails after the swap), and *err can be non-zero with return 0 for most failures.
note: slice cut head (function at 259-443, slice 277-528). reviewer round 15 right: move_extent.c:404 can set a negative *err after the swap while replaced_count is returned at 422 unchanged.

name: dx_probe
prose: Precondition: dir is an indexed (htree) directory inode; frame_in points to caller-owned storage for EXT4_HTREE_LEVEL struct dx_frame; fname is NULL or a filename whose hinfo and name are used, hinfo is used for the hash result when fname is NULL (namei.c:778-936, static). Postcondition: returns a struct dx_frame pointer or an error pointer; the return statements are line 793, 907 and 935. It zeroes all of frame_in, then reads directory block 0 with ext4_read_dirblock(dir, 0, INDEX); on error it returns that error pointer cast to a frame pointer (793) without any release. Otherwise it validates the root: an unrecognised hash_version (not TEA, HALF_MD4, LEGACY or SIPHASH), SIPHASH mismatched with ext4_hash_in_dirent, unused_flags bit 0 set, indirect_levels at or above ext4_dir_htree_level(), or an entries limit different from dx_root_limit each emit a warning and go to fail. It sets hinfo (hash version adjusted by s_hash_unsigned for versions up to TEA, seed from the superblock) and, when fname has a name and the directory is not both encrypted and casefolded, calls ext4fs_dirhash, whose negative result is returned as ERR_PTR(ret) through fail. It then descends the tree: at each level it checks count != 0 and count <= limit, binary-searches the entries for the last entry whose hash does not exceed the target, records entries and at in the current frame, fails on a cycle (a block number equal to one already used at an upper level), and returns frame at 907 once ++level exceeds indirect (the deepest frame, with all frames from frame_in up to it holding buffer heads that the caller must release). For a lower level it reads the next block with ext4_read_dirblock; on error ret_err is that error, the frame's bh is set NULL and it goes to fail; a node limit different from dx_node_limit also goes to fail. fail: brelses the buffer head of every frame from the current one down to frame_in, then, if ret_err is still the initial ERR_PTR(ERR_BAD_DX_DIR) (the value is used directly, not negated), warns 'Corrupt directory, running e2fsck is recommended'; returns ret_err (935), which is ERR_PTR(ERR_BAD_DX_DIR), the dirhash error or the read error. The caller must release the buffers only on success.

name: ext4_orphan_cleanup
prose: Precondition: sb is a mounted ext4 superblock and es its on-disk superblock image; called at mount or remount time (orphan.c:378-507, returns void). Postcondition: returns nothing, with these early returns that leave sb->s_flags as it was: (1) at 393 when es->s_last_orphan is 0 and the orphan file is empty; (2) at 399 when the block device is read-only (error message); (3) at 406 when ext4_feature_set_ok(sb, 0) fails; (4) at 417 when EXT4_ERROR_FS is set in s_mount_state, after setting es->s_last_orphan = 0 only if it was non-zero and the mount is not read-only (the list is not cleared on a read-only mount). Otherwise it clears SB_RDONLY from sb->s_flags if set, and with CONFIG_QUOTA turns on quotas (ext4_enable_quotas for the quota feature when the mount was read-only, and ext4_quota_on_mount for each journaled-quota name), recording quota_update if any succeeded (failures only log). It then loops while es->s_last_orphan is non-zero: if EXT4_ERROR_FS has become set it sets es->s_last_orphan = 0 and stops; it calls ext4_orphan_get on the head inode number, and if that returns an error pointer it sets es->s_last_orphan = 0 and stops; otherwise it links the inode into sbi->s_orphan and calls ext4_process_orphan. It then walks every slot of the orphan-file blocks, skipping zero slots and inodes for which ext4_orphan_get fails, marks the inode ORPHAN_FILE, records its index and calls ext4_process_orphan. ext4_process_orphan (orphan.c:321-359) does dquot_initialize; if inode->i_nlink is non-zero it truncates the page cache and calls ext4_truncate under inode_lock (on failure ext4_orphan_del(NULL, inode) and ext4_std_error) and counts a truncate, otherwise it only counts an orphan (deleted by the final iput); then it calls iput(inode). After the loops it logs the counts of deleted orphan inodes and cleaned-up truncates when non-zero, turns off quotas (dquot_quota_off for each type with an open file) if quota_update was set, restores sb->s_flags to the original value (506), and returns. es->s_last_orphan is not guaranteed to be 0 at exit by this function itself: the loop ends when the chain ends, an error is hit (cleared explicitly) or the error state stops it.

name: ext4_resize_fs
prose: Precondition: sb is a mounted ext4 superblock and n_blocks_count is the requested new size in blocks; the caller serialises resizes (resize.c:1997-2193). Postcondition: returns an int, with these return points: -ENOSPC at 2020 if ext4_sb_bread of block n_blocks_count - 1 fails (resize aborted, no state changed); -EINVAL at 2043 if the requested size is below the current size (shrinking is not supported); 0 at 2048 if it equals the current size; -EINVAL at 2053 if the last group number would overflow the inode count; -EINVAL at 2066 if the resize_inode and meta_bg features are both enabled (ext4_error); PTR_ERR(resize_inode) at 2085 if ext4_iget of EXT4_RESIZE_INO fails; and 'return err' at 2192 after the out label (err is 0 or the negative error). For bigalloc the size is first rounded down to a cluster boundary. With the resize_inode feature, if more descriptor blocks are needed than the reserved GDT blocks allow, the target is clamped to the reserved capacity and the original target saved in n_blocks_count_retry. If there is no resize inode and no meta_bg and more descriptor blocks are needed (or the target equals the current size), ext4_convert_meta_bg is run (error: goto out), and a saved retry target is reinstated and the function goes back to retry. If the last group would be too small for its metadata the target is cut back to the start of that group and it goes to retry (dropping resize_inode). The last group is then extended with ext4_group_extend_no_check when add > 0 (error: goto out); if the block count already equals the target and no retry is pending it goes to out. Otherwise it allocates the flex_bg array and group info (errors: out), allocates flex_gd (-ENOMEM: out) and loops over ext4_setup_next_flex_gd: each round calls ext4_alloc_group_tables, and if that returns non-zero the loop breaks WITHOUT setting err (so err stays 0 and the function can return 0 without having grown the filesystem further), else err = ext4_flex_group_add and an error breaks the loop. If err is 0 and a retry target is pending it frees flex_gd, drops resize_inode and goes to retry (this also happens after the alloc_group_tables break). out: frees flex_gd, iputs resize_inode if set, warns if err is non-zero, logs the final size and returns err.

name: ext4_xattr_set_handle
prose: Precondition: inode is an ext4 inode; handle is a journal handle (possibly not a real journal handle) with enough credits, name is the attribute name (non-NULL expected), value is the new value or NULL to remove, value_len its length, name_index the namespace index, flags may hold XATTR_CREATE or XATTR_REPLACE; the caller must not hold the inode's xattr lock because the function takes it itself (xattr.c:2351-2501). Postcondition: returns an int through three return statements: -EINVAL at 2372 if name is NULL, -ERANGE at 2374 if strlen(name) > 255, and 'return error' at 2500 after the cleanup label; 0 on success, a negative errno otherwise. It takes ext4_write_lock_xattr(inode, &no_expand). If the handle is valid it reads the xattr block (error: cleanup), computes the credits needed via __ext4_xattr_set_credits and fails with -ENOSPC if the handle has fewer buffer credits. It then reserves the inode for writing (ext4_reserve_inode_write, error: cleanup); if EXT4_STATE_NEW it zeroes the raw inode and clears the state; it looks the attribute up first in the in-inode body (ext4_xattr_ibody_find) and, if not found there, in the block (ext4_xattr_block_find), errors going to cleanup. If it exists nowhere: -ENODATA if XATTR_REPLACE; otherwise 0 with nothing to do when value is NULL (removing an absent attribute returns 0 and changes nothing); if it exists and XATTR_CREATE is set: -EEXIST. Removal (value NULL) calls ext4_xattr_ibody_set or ext4_xattr_block_set, whichever holds it. Setting: if the existing value (in the body or the block) is identical (ext4_xattr_value_same) it goes to cleanup with error 0 and neither ctime nor i_version is updated; otherwise, when the ea_inode feature is on and the value is large, i.in_inode is set; it tries ext4_xattr_ibody_set, then removes a copy from the block if one existed; on -ENOSPC it sets the value in the block (re-finding the block first when needed) and removes the in-body copy if present, and if the block set also returns -ENOSPC it retries once with the value stored in an EA inode (retry_inode) when the feature is on and it was not already. On success (error == 0) it calls ext4_xattr_update_super_block, sets ctime to now, increments i_version, clears no_expand when removing, calls ext4_mark_iloc_dirty (whose error becomes the return value even though earlier steps already changed the inode) and ext4_handle_sync for IS_SYNC inodes. In every case reaching line 2494, ext4_fc_mark_ineligible(..., EXT4_FC_REASON_XATTR, handle) is called. cleanup: brelse of is.iloc.bh and bs.bh and ext4_write_unlock_xattr. Failures after the first step of a two-step update (body then block, or block then body) or a failure of ext4_mark_iloc_dirty can leave an earlier modification in the journalled buffers; the function does not roll it back.

name: __f2fs_is_valid_blkaddr
prose: Precondition: sbi is a valid f2fs_sb_info, blkaddr is a block address, type is one of META_NAT, META_SIT, META_SSA, META_CP, META_POR, DATA_GENERIC, DATA_GENERIC_ENHANCE, DATA_GENERIC_ENHANCE_READ, DATA_GENERIC_ENHANCE_UPDATE or META_GENERIC (checkpoint.c:174-233, static bool). Postcondition: returns true or false; any other type value hits BUG(). By type: META_NAT always returns true (no check). META_SIT: false if blkaddr >= SIT_BLK_CNT(sbi), else true. META_SSA: false if blkaddr >= MAIN_BLKADDR(sbi) or < SM_I(sbi)->ssa_blkaddr, else true. META_CP: false if blkaddr >= SIT_I(sbi)->sit_base_addr or < __start_cp_addr(sbi), else true. META_POR: false if blkaddr >= MAX_BLKADDR(sbi) or < MAIN_BLKADDR(sbi), else true. These four out-of-range cases (check_only label) return false with no message or side effect. Data types: if blkaddr is outside [MAIN_BLKADDR, MAX_BLKADDR): if f2fs_cp_error(sbi) it returns false silently (line 208); otherwise it logs a warning, sets SBI_NEED_FSCK, calls dump_stack(), then (label err) calls f2fs_handle_error(sbi, ERROR_INVALID_BLKADDR) and returns false. If the address is in range it returns the result of __is_bitmap_valid(sbi, blkaddr, type) (line 216). META_GENERIC: false (via err, so with f2fs_handle_error(ERROR_INVALID_BLKADDR)) if blkaddr < SEG0_BLKADDR(sbi) or >= MAIN_BLKADDR(sbi), else true.
note: unreviewed in the last round; checked against checkpoint.c:174-233. Round 1 reviewer right (cp_error returns false silently at 207-208), round 2 reviewer right (dump_stack at 213 for out-of-range data). Slice is 1-267 but the function is at 174-233 (included).
